messages:
mira: quick idea for continuous batching: split the monolith into "ingress" (accept + cheap accounting) and "packer" (windowing + batch assembly). want to surface tradeoffs before an RFC.

devin: ok. what are we trying to improve vs current single-queue design?

mira: main goals: reduce coupling (admit logic vs batch build), make preemption explicit, and limit the amount of per-request state kept while still enabling kv-cache pinning when a packer decides to materialize.

ash: how do you prevent the ingress from buffering unlimited requests if packers are slow?

mira: two levers: (1) compact queue entries (opaque token + tiny shape hint + tenant id) and (2) a soft reservation ledger per-tenant. Enqueue returns either accepted + token or rejected. rejected -> fallback tier. accepted entries are reclaimable under overload.

ravi: tokens need lifecycle semantics. propose lease token with expiry and three states: queued, claimed, pinned. packer claims tokens for a batch, then promotes a subset to pinned (kv cache pin). if packer dies, leases expire and ingress reclaims.

devin: what's in shape_hint? just estimated token_count and priority? also a deadline?

mira: yes: {max_tokens_est, priority_bucket, deadline_ms, trace_id}. keep small. packer must make decisions only from hints until it claims and decodes.

pat: routing implication: current flow is per-GPU queue. if ingress is global we either forward pointers to remote packer or replicate small metadata. network hops add latency. prefer staged rollout: start with co-located ingress+packer per-worker, then enable cross-node packers.

ash: agree staged rollout. also suggest ingress expose a short API: Enqueue(tenant, hint) -> (accepted, token), Cancel(token). packer: PeekCandidates(max_tokens) -> [token], Pin(token) -> success/fail, Release(token).

mira: added constraint: token must include debug_trace and checksum so ops can correlate. also telemetry: reservation.used, reservation.reclaimed, ingress.queue_depth_by_tenant, packer.fill_rate.

ravi: reclaim policy: packer should preferentially reclaim reclaimable low-priority tokens when under pressure. but we need fairness: tenants with sustained load shouldn't get starved by repeated reclaim. ledger should track decaying usage credits.

devin: headroom oscillation is a real risk if ingress adapts aggressively to packer fill_rate. add dampening and expose expected_fill_rate from packer. suggest ingress smoothing window of ~500ms for aggressiveness tuning.

mira: good call. also circuit breaker for pathological long tails: if a token is repeatedly pinned-extended beyond some threshold, mark it as "long-tail" and force eviction or move to dedicated slow-path execution so short requests remain fast.

pat: operational notes: implement in two phases: (A) in-process split with shared memory ledger and no remote routing; (B) enable remote packer routing + pointer forwarding. run canary on single GPU pool.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: batcher-split/phase-a -> canary at 04:00 UTC

nash: API versioning: expose both old enqueue and new enqueue side-by-side for backward compatibility. we can route traffic by feature-flag.

ravi: failure modes to test: packer crash, token loss, ledger inconsistency, network partition when using remote packers. we need deterministic cleanup routines that reclaim leases on restart.

devin: i'll take the spike to build token format + simple ledger shim. also will write a sim for headroom oscillation. expect results in 3 days.

mira: i'll draft RFC with proto sketches and rollout checklist (metrics, ops runbook, circuit breaker thresholds). ping me if you want to pair on the sim. :+1:

pat: thumbs up. let's avoid changing kv-cache pin interfaces in this first phase; treat pin as optional and only used when packer is local.

mira: noted. keeping kv pin as a later opt-in reduces blast radius. closing this thread 7:15am7. RFC link to follow.
